QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_44

question.text: Ujala Solar Foundation (a Section 8 company classified as an NPO) has attracted interest from 'Bharat Impact Fund I', an EXISTING Social Impact Fund not launched exclusively for SSE-listed NPOs. If Bharat Impact Fund I has investable funds of Rs 500 crore, what is the MAXIMUM amount it may invest in securities of NPOs registered or listed on an SSE?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook p.71, an existing Social Impact Fund may invest up to 25% of its investable funds in securities of NPOs registered or listed on a social stock exchange. 25% of Rs 500 crore equals Rs 125 crore. The 100% threshold applies only to SIFs launched exclusively for SSE-registered or listed NPOs. The Trap: Option B (75%) confuses this with a separate FPE-side rule. Option C (100%) applies only to SIFs launched exclusively for SSE-registered or listed NPOs. Option D invents a 5% cap. Note: Per p.56, Section 8 companies are classified as NPOs, so the NPO-side 25% cap is the applicable rule here.
